label: <DEL> delimiter in short sequences (L<=6), plus early 1/c/j inputs
explanation: Mainly a delimiter-step unit: about 85% of activation mass is on the <DEL> input. It fires there in 48% of sequences overall, nearly always when L<=5 (98% precision) and often at L=6, but rarely for L>=7. Activation is largest for the shortest sequences: all top examples are L=3-4. The secondary component (about 11% of mass, lower magnitude) is the original-phase inputs 1, c, j (and more weakly t) at positions 2-3. It is essentially silent in the copy phase (0.4% of mass), at t=0-1, and on other tokens in the original phase. Most misses are weak activations on <DEL> in long sequences.

issues: I checked the claims against the dev split and they hold. <DEL> carries 85.4% of activation mass and the unit fires at <DEL> in 48.4% of sequences. The <DEL> & L<=5 clause alone has precision 0.983. At L=6 the unit fires on <DEL> 67% of the time, at L>=7 only 8%. The copy phase holds 0.4% of mass, and the unit is never active at t=0 and almost never at t=1.

The original-phase clause holds about 13% of mass, a little above the stated 11%. Its two positions behave very differently. At t==2 it is reliable: inputs 1/c/j have precision 0.92. At t==3 most predicted steps do not fire (precision 0.37). Restricting t=3 to steps where no 1/c/j/t was seen earlier raises this only to 0.45. So '1/c/j at positions 2-3' overstates position 3, which is a weak and inconsistent part.
Input t at t=2 fires 49% of the time and is left out of the predicate. The explanation does mention it ('t more weakly'), so this is a small omission, not a mistake.

At L=6, about 33% of <DEL> steps do not fire. Whether the sequence contains 1/c/j makes no difference (0.65 vs 0.70), so these misses look like a graded fall-off with length rather than a missing content rule.

The test-split misses show no systematic class. Missed activations hold 3.7% of mass and are mostly weak <DEL> firing at L>=7 plus some t/c inputs. False positives are mostly L=6 <DEL> steps and 1/c/j at t=3.

Small alternatives barely change the score. Dropping the t=3 part gives test F1 0.856 (P 0.889, R 0.825). Keeping t=3 only when no 1/c/j/t came before gives test F1 0.859. The original predicate scores 0.851, so it is near the best simple description.
skeptic.revised_label: <DEL> delimiter in short sequences (L<=6, strongest for L<=4), plus 1/c/j inputs at position 2 (weaker at 3)
skeptic.better_predicate: ((phase == 1) & (L <= 6)) | ((phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("1"), tok("c"), tok("j")]) & (t == 2)) | ((phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("1"), tok("c"), tok("j")]) & (t == 3) & ~seen([tok("1"), tok("c"), tok("j"), tok("t")]))

final_label: <DEL> delimiter in short sequences (L<=6, strongest for L<=4), plus 1/c/j inputs at position 2 (weaker at 3)
